title: Sleep trait predicted effector genes in pancreatic islets (Lasconi C et al. 2022)
bodyHtml:
This table presents putative effector genes list for sleep-associated loci in metabolic cell types, from the study:

Variant-to-gene-mapping analyses reveal a role for pancreatic islet cells in conferring genetic susceptibility to sleep-related traits.
Lasconi C, et al.
Sleep. 2022 Aug;45(8): zsac109. doi: https://doi.org/10.1093/sleep/zsac109 
PMID: 35537191

This study investigated and added to the growing evidence confirming the genetic relationship between metabolic syndrome and sleep disturbances. They looked at the potential role of sleep-trait associated genetic loci in metabolic disorders by assessing the effect sizes of these loci on pancreatic α- and β-cells. They conducted this assessment by doing linkage disequilibrium analysis using publicly available GWAS summary statistics, and functional follow-up with enrichment analysis of sleep-trait associated SNPs in promoter-interacting open chromatin regions within α- and β-cells by meta-analyzing their own ATAC-seq and high-resolution promoter-focused Capture C data with public GWAS reports. Ultimately, they were able to identify 76 putative effector genes physically interacting with aforementioned sleep loci, specifically for insomnia, short sleep, long sleep, and morningness, in EndoC-βH1 and α-cells and characterize the pathways in which these genes are implicated.
